learningObjective: Trace a patch from its two-dimensional image location into the ordered ViT token sequence and explain why a position vector is added to every patch embedding before self-attention.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can preserve the correspondence between a two-dimensional patch grid, row-major sequence order, per-token vector addition, and the class token in one spatial trace. A four-patch toy image exposes the representation change without reproducing the full paper architecture.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because automatic graph layout cannot align exact image-grid locations with their corresponding sequence positions, and the mechanism is a reshape rather than a branching process.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected because fixed cells, labels, arrows, and aligned token rows make the two-dimensional-to-one-dimensional mapping and position-vector addition directly inspectable.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because tables can enumerate patches and tokens but cannot show the same patch simultaneously as a region in the image and an item in the sequence as directly.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because clicking patches would hide simultaneous correspondences and add state when four visible patches are enough to establish the invariant.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the original paper's Figure 1 contains a much denser end-to-end architecture and the arXiv record does not establish a permissive figure-reuse license. No external artwork, wording, coordinates, or layout is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the prose asks readers to mentally perform a representation change from a two-dimensional image grid to a one-dimensional token sequence while also remembering that positional vectors restore location information.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-indexed page by page for the exact terms vision transformer, ViT, image patch, patch embedding, patchify, image, positional embedding, and self-attention. Page 50 is the only exact ViT match, and pages 49-51 were extracted as its complete immediate neighborhood. The dedicated computer-vision neighborhood on pages 146-150 was also extracted because it supplies the deck's image and CNN context. No deck slide shows ViT patchification or the two-dimensional-grid-to-token-sequence transformation.

sources.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for splitting an image into fixed-size non-overlapping patches, flattening and linearly projecting them, prepending a learned class token, adding learned one-dimensional positional embeddings, and applying a standard transformer encoder.
sources.license: The arXiv record does not identify a permissive third-party figure license. The paper is cited for technical verification only; no figure, equation layout, prose, result, or visual composition is reproduced.

sources.title: Google Research Vision Transformer reference implementation
sources.usage: Used as the official reference implementation to verify patch projection by a kernel and stride equal to patch size, reshape from an embedding grid to a sequence, class-token concatenation, positional-vector addition, and class-token selection after the encoder.
sources.license: The repository is Apache-2.0 licensed. No source code, comments, example image, model weights, or artwork is copied; only public tensor semantics are cited.

sources.title: Torchvision VisionTransformer implementation
sources.usage: Used as an independent official implementation to cross-check the sequence length formula, non-overlapping convolutional patch projection, grid flattening order, class-token prepend, learned positional embedding, and classifier use of sequence position zero.
sources.license: Torchvision is BSD-3-Clause licensed. No code, documentation prose, model data, or artwork is reused; the implementation only corroborates tensor shapes and operation order.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is what is preserved and what must be reintroduced when ViT turns space into a sequence. In the original architecture, a patch x_p^i is flattened and projected to d dimensions; it occupies a fixed sequence slot, receives the learned positional vector for that slot, and participates in ordinary self-attention. A class token occupies slot zero and receives its own position vector. The toy figure uses a 4 by 4 RGB image divided into four non-overlapping 2 by 2 patches: each flattened patch has 2 times 2 times 3 equals 12 values, each projection has width d, and the encoder receives five tokens including CLS. Without positional embeddings, permuting patch tokens would permute their encoder outputs while leaving the class-token output invariant, so patch location would not be available to the classifier.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages, inspected the sole ViT mention and the full image-model neighborhood, and checked the primary paper plus official Google and Torchvision implementations before selecting an original patch-to-token SVG.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description stating the toy image dimensions, four patch locations, row-major token order, projection shapes, positional additions, class token, and encoder input length. Patch numbers, row-and-column labels, arrows, plus signs, and matching text carry every correspondence without relying on color. The compact 360-unit viewBox has no minimum width and uses established text sizes for readability at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules force a light high-contrast palette and keep the figure together.
